playbook.intent: A recurring internal or client process is visibly costing more time and rework than anyone budgeted for, and the argument about why keeps restarting because nobody has measured it. It ends when the work runs on the redesigned path, the number that motivated the whole effort has moved against a measured starting point, and someone inside the business — not the analyst who was brought in — owns the review that keeps it there.
playbook.scope: BA-led continuous improvement programme on an existing internal or client process: measure baseline, design future state, pilot, roll out, lock in benefits. End state — measurable KPI shift with sustained governance after BA leaves.

success-criteria.criterion: Cycle time, rework rate and hand-off count for the process are measured from real cases, not from what the process owner believes happens
The future-state design names each hand-off it removes and each control it deliberately keeps, and the sponsor has signed the version that says so
A pilot ran the redesigned path on live volume, and the call to scale it or drop it was argued from the pilot's numbers
Roll-out covers the whole case population the redesign was scoped for, with a documented fallback for the exceptions it was not
The target metric has moved against the measured starting point and held through at least one full reporting period after roll-out
The benefit is booked against a named budget line or a freed-capacity figure that finance recognises
A named person inside the business owns the process metric and has run the review once without the analyst in the room
